title: Space-Fillers and Lattice Moves: Which Solids Fill Space, Which Only Together, and Which Hold by Shape Alone
description: Space-Fillers and Lattice Moves, Version 1: the volume that gathers DICTO's results on which solids fill space alone, which only together, and which hold by shape alone. Opening: What This Book Shows. Chapter 1, The Dehn Test Picks Out the Lone Tilers of Two Sweeps: on the sweep from the octahedron to the cube the Dehn invariant is 24√2(3 − 2μ) ⊗ β and then −24√2(3 − μ) ⊗ β, zero exactly at Kelvin's truncated octahedron and the cube; on the sweep from the rhombic dodecahedron to the cuboctahedron it vanishes for 1 ≤ μ ≤ 4/3 and at the B3 permutohedron (μ = 5/3), and the local count of edge angles leaves only the rhombic dodecahedron; on the tetrahedron sweep it picks the known β-tin tiler. Chapter 2, Truncated Tetrahedra That Fill Space: Dehn Zero Is the Octet's Own Ratio: a tetrahedron with corner cuts c is Dehn-zero exactly when Σc = 1, which is the tetrahedron cut by a translate of twice its inverse, and for whole-layer cuts exactly the octet's ratio of two tetrahedra per octahedron; all twelve integer cases with n ≤ 5 and one at n = 8 tile space, two pieces per period (SAT exact cover); conjecture for every rational cut; the seven golden Dehn-zero cuts listed exactly. Chapter 3, The Admiral Cap Network: Only the Mixture Fills, and Never Face to Face: the face pyramid, the icosahedron and DICTO's Admiral Cap each have nonzero Dehn invariant; at most 8 of 12 shared edges match round any corner; the best arrangements are layers with one free flip per layer. Chapter 4, Held by Shape Alone: in a (111) layer of the octet every octahedron is locked and every tetrahedron free; in the Admiral layer of #47 every Admiral Cap and icosahedron is locked against small slides and twists. Appendix: the Dehn screen, exact cover on the octet and the interlocking test, with their calibrations.
notes: Version 1: first version. Cover by DICTO to follow.
